label: Company-fleets override register: every local adaptation of an upstream source. Revisions are pinned from sources/ledger.json; `bin/fleet overrides` reports drift.

overrides.requirement: Existing top-level router and one-dispatcher rule prevail over imported orchestration defaults.
overrides.reason: Each imported orchestrator picks and starts work from its own queue, so two of them could run one workload.
overrides.precedence: The router (Claude Code plus credit-routing) picks the workload; the factory-rig lease decides who holds it; a fleet coordinator claims but never dispatches; agency-agents' orchestrator is not installed.
overrides.scope: Every fleet workload and every workflow run.
overrides.retire_when: A backend offers cross-backend ownership with the same fencing guarantee as the factory-rig lease.

overrides.requirement: Existing PM, verification, memory, publishing, provider, and permissions contracts remain authoritative.
overrides.reason: Imported packages describe their own project-management, verification, memory and publishing flows that would compete with the rig's.
overrides.precedence: factory-rig contracts and merge gate, the one tracker per project, the rig's provider wrappers and Claude Code permission settings win; fleet skills only add checks inside them.
overrides.retire_when: Never while the rig keeps one PM and gate layer; revisit if the rig adopts an imported PM layer as canonical.

overrides.reason: samber's kickoff router and Alireza's prompt hook each route work on their own; inside the rig they may only suggest skills within one fleet workload.
overrides.precedence: A domain router runs only after the fleet coordinator claimed the workload, and only names skills; `dispatch` is false on every role.
overrides.scope: DevRel, corporate and any fleet that adopts an upstream router skill.
overrides.owner: DevRel fleet for samber; foundation for the dispatch rule
overrides.retire_when: An upstream router exposes a bounded mode that the rig can check mechanically.

overrides.requirement: Generic numeric targets become explicit hypotheses or locally calibrated policies.
overrides.reason: Role seeds and advisors state universal targets (load times, margins, ratios) with no local baseline.
overrides.precedence: A target is a hypothesis with its proposer and date until a local measurement calibrates it; an unmet target stays unmet.
overrides.scope: Hosting targets, agency estimates, corporate finance and capacity plans.
overrides.owner: Hosting fleet for service targets; corporate fleet for finance
overrides.retire_when: Each target has a calibrated local policy with its own evidence.

overrides.requirement: Script outputs include assumptions and applicability; queueing or financial models do not justify false precision.
overrides.reason: Upstream calculators print point estimates with no stated assumptions, and three of them crash on malformed input (sources/README.md, Qualification).
overrides.precedence: Every handoff carries an assumptions list; a calculator result enters a decision only with its assumptions and the range it holds for.
overrides.scope: Corporate finance, capacity and pricing; hosting measurements.
overrides.retire_when: The upstream scripts print assumptions and validate input themselves; recheck on each upgrade.

overrides.requirement: Personas cannot fabricate experience, certification, authority, customer quotes, or research findings.
overrides.reason: Agency Agents profiles invent years of experience; a persona with a credential reads as authority the rig does not have.
overrides.precedence: A role persona is a viewpoint; the validator and each fleet's persona evals reject credentials, employers and invented findings.
overrides.owner: Foundation workstream (schema) and each fleet (persona evals)
overrides.retire_when: Never; this is a standing rule.

overrides.requirement: Simulated reviews cannot replace required human research, language review, learner data, or external assessment.
overrides.reason: The DaRL pipeline's simulated student and generated reviews look like evidence of learning or usability.
overrides.precedence: A workflow step marked human-data stops the run; linguistic review stays `required`; generated calibration sets are practice only.
overrides.scope: Localization, developer education, BCIT units, trainer development, compliance assessment.
overrides.retire_when: Never; real human data replaces the boundary only when a person supplies it.

overrides.requirement: Company-specific tools and paths are adapted through native interfaces.
overrides.reason: Kanopi assumes DDEV, Teamwork and Snyk and HashiCorp's skill applies real infrastructure; none of that exists or is authorized here.
overrides.precedence: A step uses the project's actual tools through the platform adapter; terraform runs only in plan mode or with mock providers.
overrides.scope: Agency engineering, product releases, hosting operations.
overrides.retire_when: A project names its tools and the adapter resolves them without a manual step.

overrides.requirement: Duplicate skill names receive unambiguous selection or namespaced wrappers.
overrides.reason: These names also ship in synced plugins, so a name alone does not say which copy loads.
overrides.precedence: Roles load a skill by path (resolve returns skills/<id>/SKILL.md); a skill id is registered in one fleet only; the hidden rig copies never compete in the model's list.
overrides.retire_when: Claude Code namespaces plugin and rig skills so names cannot collide.

overrides.requirement: Standards access and redistribution rights are recorded before ingestion.
overrides.reason: Standards bodies (NBEA, NOCTI, ISTE, CSTA) restrict access and redistribution, and some skill text is share-alike.
overrides.precedence: A standard without recorded edition, access and license is a gap, never an alignment; NBEA stays blocked until a person records them.
overrides.scope: BCIT education, instructional design and every imported skill.
overrides.owner: Education fleet (standards) and sources workstream (skill licenses)
overrides.retire_when: Never; each new source records its rights first.

overrides.requirement: Marketing loops stage outputs and respect actual scheduling/send authority.
overrides.reason: Upstream marketing procedures end in scheduling and sending; the rig has no send authority.
overrides.precedence: Marketing steps run with publication staged-only and external_actions draft-only; a send needs a named human holding that authority.
overrides.scope: Corporate marketing, lifecycle email, launch campaigns.
overrides.retire_when: Never while no send authority is delegated to an agent.

overrides.requirement: Client, community, and education records keep their access boundaries.
overrides.reason: Upstream community and teaching skills assume one shared context; the rig serves several tenants, moderation cases and classrooms.
overrides.precedence: A record stays in its tenant unless public, an approved abstraction, or granted by a named human; student records and moderation cases need the grant.
overrides.scope: Every handoff and every fleet that holds tenant records.
overrides.retire_when: Never; this is a standing rule.

overrides.reason: Upstream installers copy skills into Codex directories and some skills assume an MCP server or account that only one harness has.
overrides.precedence: The ledger records side effects and native-tool needs per repository; installers are read, never run; Codex mounts come only from your machine's mount list.
overrides.retire_when: A behavior check runs the same skill under Claude and Codex and records both.

overrides.requirement: Upstream upgrades trigger affected compatibility checks.
overrides.reason: Upstream trees move (WordPress tracks trunk); a silent upgrade could change a skill a fleet relies on.
overrides.precedence: After skill-sync applies an upgrade, verify_sources reports tree drift and `fleet overrides` reports every override whose pinned upstream revision moved; the affected fleet evals rerun before the override is re-pinned.
overrides.scope: Every override in this register and every ledger repository.
overrides.retire_when: Never; it is the update check itself.
